lxc_b5d33e78db51ceac.text: Watermelon began in Africa, but people changed it over thousands of years.

lxc_34dfe63bcda78499.text: Today, the same fruit can be a snack, a drink, a food with cheese, or a special local shape.

lxc_7641c25693c8d84b.text: A pale melon from Sudan called the Kordofan melon is the closest known relative of today's watermelon.

lxc_ff0609929fe9a74b.text: It may be one of its ancestors.

lxc_46b56b484e1fbfff.text: Pictures in ancient Egyptian tombs suggest that people ate a watermelon-like fruit more than 4,000 years ago.

lxc_c035fb35dfdce0df.text: Those early fruits were not always bright red or very sweet.

lxc_257e4ae57ed603dc.text: Farmers saved seeds from fruit with qualities they liked.

lxc_f9d53edeebf4225f.text: Over many generations, watermelon became sweeter, and red flesh became common.

lxc_848158f937722df5.text: This change took a very long time.

lxc_9a313cae7ae0e481.text: In China, people do not only enjoy the red flesh.

lxc_85bf1ba12f917c22.text: Roasted watermelon seeds are also a popular snack.

lxc_1aacff6ea2992132.text: Some farmers grow special seeded watermelons mainly for their seeds.

lxc_bf6718d8ac85bad9.text: After the fruit is ready, the seeds are collected and roasted.

lxc_9788107f9691cf96.text: People open the hard shell and eat the small part inside.

lxc_ebcb3ab1e3e6512a.text: This takes time, so the snack can be enjoyed slowly while people talk or rest.

lxc_c25488eff34781f3.text: One plant can therefore give people two very different foods: juicy fruit and dry, crunchy seeds.

lxc_f964ce05a2478e04.text: Some people in Turkiye eat cold watermelon with white cheese in summer.

lxc_88d4ca8a95761001.text: The fruit is sweet and juicy, but the cheese is salty.

lxc_d30fa6e433366161.text: The two different tastes can work well together.

lxc_50b430232cbd3333.text: Size can also give watermelon a special meaning.

lxc_3377cddf680375e8.text: Diyarbakir holds a culture and watermelon festival with a competition for very large local fruit.

lxc_464827f5bc6ac5f9.text: Watermelons in this competition can weigh between 15 and 70 kilograms.

lxc_99d70c271a8f26af.text: The event celebrates local farming and pride.

lxc_7b6db69e8bf7f318.text: This example connects a simple summer meal with a long farming tradition.

lxc_aaf658907fc03c96.text: In Mexico, watermelon can become a cold drink called agua fresca.

lxc_704f8a4b665edbc1.text: Aguas frescas are an important part of Mexican food culture.

lxc_71a6ab69ebcf2f3a.text: People make different kinds with fruit or seeds, water, ice, and sometimes sugar.

lxc_299bee1d0b7a6c54.text: For a watermelon version, the fruit is mixed with water and served cold.

lxc_47b0a83881a86aa0.text: Recipes can change from one family or shop to another.

lxc_c6bfa6c0e755eaff.text: This drink is easy to share from a large container on a hot day.

lxc_1d8d31c488549d55.text: Here, people enjoy the fresh taste without eating a slice.

lxc_cbd3fe8f58f50fc8.text: Most people eat the soft flesh and throw away the rind.

lxc_ac5ec29d2fae2ad3.text: In parts of the southern United States, however, people make pickles from the pale part of the rind.

lxc_371e7b0000e42bcb.text: They first remove the fruit and the hard dark-green skin.

lxc_e345b0342cdbe00e.text: The crisp pale rind can then be prepared as a pickle.

lxc_550c4a82111541c6.text: Home cooks and small producers have kept this food tradition alive.

lxc_398b320af1ed39bc.text: It turns a part that often becomes waste into something people can eat.

lxc_561ad96d341e9d51.text: The watermelon is not only a sweet dessert anymore.

lxc_501308d443048ef2.text: In Zentsuji City in Kagawa, Japan, some farmers grow cube-shaped watermelons.

lxc_101078d0756cf8a5.text: They place the young fruit inside special containers as it grows.

lxc_7045124082f32410.text: Local farmers have developed this skill since the late 1960s.

lxc_886e314018cf8a70.text: The regular shape and beautiful stripes make these watermelons unusual, and they can sell for high prices.

lxc_9a42eca829fe0f56.text: People may value them as local gifts or display pieces.

lxc_d1374c57ca1711b8.text: Their shape does not mean that they taste better.

lxc_ceb600173c38d615.text: Like roasted seeds, cheese, drinks, and pickles, the square fruit shows that people can give the same plant very different meanings.
